messages:
Ravi: Proposal: run a controlled "shadow+split" experiment for EU tenant batches to validate resident-write behavior without committing to resident storage. Goal: catch policy regressions and consent mismatches before full cutover. Low blast, observable. Thoughts? :seedling:

Elaine: Sounds good. Two immediate asks: 1) ensure shadow copies obey consent headers (X-Consent-Token) 2) strip or hash any PII in shadow payloads by default. We can't risk unredacted copies leaving region.

Marco: Operational plan sketch: proxy will 98% route to primary path, 2% to resident-shadow with headers: X-Shadow: true, X-Policy: eu-shadow-v1. Resident path will accept but not commit (dry-run). We'll compare response codes + normalized outputs.

Zoe: Telemetry required: shadow_mismatch_count, shadow_request_latency_p95, shadow_resource_cpu. Also emit tenant-scoped diffs and comparator_score. Create an alert if mismatch_rate > 0.05% over 15m.

Ravi: Good list. I also want a safety circuit: if shadow_resource_cpu > 70% OR shadow_latency_p95 rises by >200ms above baseline, disable shadow routing automatically. ops-bot can handle the revert.

Marco: Sample proxy config (pseudo):
```yaml
- id: eu-shadow-v1
  match: tenant_region == "eu" and tenant_id =~ "t-2.*"
  split:
    - weight: 98
      route: primary
    - weight: 2
      route: eu-shadow-dry
  headers:
    - set: X-Shadow: "true"
    - set: X-Policy: "eu-shadow-v1"
```

Elaine: Privacy note: privacy-bot will attach a retention tag to all shadow logs (retention_days=7) and add an audit flag. Also require data-hash header so we can prove we sanitized payloads. privacy-bot: pls confirm.

privacy-bot: Confirmed. Shadow logs will be tagged with retention=7d and mask_level=pii-hash. X-Consent-Token mandatory for EU tenants. Non-compliant requests will be dropped from shadow path and counted in shadow_noncompliant_count.

Ravi: Nice. For comparison we need a deterministic comparator lib to avoid false positives due to minor generation variance. Marco: can you wire comparator v0.3 (token-set normalized + BLEU-lite) and emit comparator_score? We'll threshold at >0.02 as suspicious.

Marco: Yes. We'll run comparator in the control plane, not in-data-plane, so minimal latency impact. Shadow responses will be buffered and compared asynchronously.

Zoe: Also add caching control: disable prefix/KV cache for shadow requests or tag hits by policy. Otherwise results look identical when cache is masking writes. We'll emit kv.cache_hits{policy=...}.

Ravi: Rollout plan: staging canary -> 5k synthetic shadowed writes -> analyze diffs -> 0.5% prod for 6 hours -> 2% for 12 hours -> 5% if stable. Revert criteria: mismatch_rate > 0.05% OR shadow_failed_rate > 0.2% OR shadow_latency_p95 delta > 200ms for 10m.

Elaine: On-call assignments: primary rollback owner Marco, secondary Ravi. Zoe owns dashboards and alerts. Privacy will run audit at each stage.

Marco: For synthetic load, use this script (adjust token):
```bash
for i in $(seq 1 5000); do
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_TOKEN" \
       -H "X-Consent-Token: eu:abc123" \
       -H "X-Region: eu-central-1" \
       -d '{"tenant":"t-2001","prompt":"probe"}' \
       https://api.staging.redwood/v1/generate > /dev/null &
done
wait
```

Zoe: ops-bot scheduled canary: proxy/eu-shadow-v1 -> canary-42 (job 30911). Dashboard: https://obs.local/canary/30911. I'll post the dashboard link in here when ready.

privacy-bot: Reminder: for EU tenants we must include consent_verifier header in audit records. Add X-Consent-Verifier: sha256(consent_token|tenant_id).

Ravi: One more edge: what about failover semantics? If resident path returns a hard error, shadow should not trigger failover logic. We must ensure shadow route never updates routing metadata or leases. It's purely observational. Marco: confirm resident-shadow is read-only dry-run with no side-effects.

Marco: Confirmed. resident-shadow route runs under a sandbox that rejects any DB COMMIT calls and returns a 202-dry-run marker. We'll also tag traces with span attribute policy=eu-shadow-v1.

Elaine: Great. If this looks clean after canary, I'd like to propose a follow-up RFC to add a "shadow mode" toggle in the control plane so customer success can request residency validation for specific tenants without infra pulls. But first: ship canary.

Ravi: Thanks everyone. Marco: open the PR with proxy rule + comparator wiring + dashboard. Zoe: ping when canary metrics are live and we'll decide go/no-go. :thumbsup:
